body:
## Summary

If `ps_formula` uses the dot (`.`), the participation model includes the outcomes and the treatment column. The result is incorrect. The function gives no message.

## Steps to reproduce

```r
library(rdborrow)
fit <- function(ps_formula) {
  analysis <- setup_analysis_primary(
    data = SyntheticData,
    trial_status_col_name = "S",
    treatment_col_name = "A",
    outcome_col_name = c("y1", "y2"),
    covariates_col_name = c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5"),
    method_weighting_obj = ec_ipw(ps_formula)
  )
  run_analysis(analysis)$results$point_estimates
}

fit("S ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5")
fit("S ~ .")
```

## Expected result

The dot means only the columns in `covariates_col_name`. Alternatively, the function stops with an error that tells the user not to use the dot.

## Actual result

```
fit("S ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5")  #> -0.197  0.470
fit("S ~ .")                       #> 0.036  0.403
```

## Cause

The internal data from `.build_analysis_df()` contains the outcomes, `S`, `A`, and the covariates. The dot means all columns other than the left side. Thus, the dot adds the outcomes and `A` to the participation model.

## Correction

Before the method fits a model, make sure that each variable on the right side of a formula is in `covariates_col_name`. Stop with an error if it is not. Either expand the dot to the covariates only, or stop with an error.

Add a test for a formula with the dot.

## Affected functions

`ec_ipw()`, `ec_aipw()`, `did_ec_ipw()`, and `did_ec_aipw()`: each formula argument.

## Related

Found by two testers in the adversarial review pilot (#101). Related to #83.
title: ps_formula with the dot adds the outcomes and the treatment to the participation model
